title: Supporting and supervising students
blurb: Know the SSSA roles for student midwives, give feedback that helps, document performance properly, and keep students inside the law on medicines.
question: A third-year student midwife asks to give a woman intramuscular pethidine in labour while her practice supervisor watches. What should the midwife say?

teach.body: SPM 5.21 asks midwives to support and supervise students, promoting reflection, giving constructive feedback, and evaluating and documenting their performance. The NMC Standards for student supervision and assessment (SSSA, 2018) separate supporting a student from assessing them. In plain English: supervisors teach and give feedback every day; assessors decide, using that feedback, whether the student has met the standard.

teach.h: The three SSSA roles for student midwives

rows.label: Who
values: Any registered health or social care professional

teach.caption: SSSA 2.7, 4.1–4.4, 6.1–6.4, 7.1–7.2, 9.1.

teach.text: The practice supervisor does not sign off proficiencies: the practice assessor does, informed by supervisors' feedback. A practice assessor cannot at the same time be the same student's practice supervisor or academic assessor. 'Mentor' and 'sign-off mentor' are the old pre-2018 roles.

teach.body: Code 9.1 asks for honest, accurate and constructive feedback; 9.4 for supporting students' learning. Give it soon, privately and specifically: what she did, the effect, and what to do next time. Balance it with genuine strengths and ask for her view. Encourage reflection by asking open questions. If there is a concern, raise it early with the practice assessor so there is time to improve; never save it for the final interview.

steps.label: Specific
steps.sub: What she did and its effect

steps.label: Balanced
steps.sub: Real strengths too; ask her view

head: Medicine
Student, under direct supervision?
teach.caption: Direct supervision by a registered midwife means present, not elsewhere on the unit.

teach.body: Jade, a third-year student, is with midwife Olu. A woman requests pethidine; Jade asks to give it while Olu watches. Olu explains that students are excluded from diamorphine, morphine and pethidine, even under supervision, so Olu gives it and talks Jade through the checks. Later, Jade gives IM oxytocin for the third stage with Olu standing beside her. That evening Olu records specific, dated feedback and asks Jade to reflect on the two medicines.

rows.label: Specific: what she did and when
Linked to the proficiency or skill
What to do next and by when
Concerns shared early with the assessor

teach.note: Practice supervisors record their observations to inform the practice assessor (SSSA 4.2–4.4).

items: Practice supervisor: any registered health or social care professional; teaches, records, raises concerns.
Practice assessor and academic assessor for midwifery students must be NMC registered midwives.
The practice assessor confirms practice proficiencies; a different academic assessor for each part.
Feedback is soon, private, specific, balanced and ends with an agreed plan; concerns go to the assessor early.
Students give Sch 17 medicines under direct supervision, but never diamorphine, morphine or pethidine.

summary: You can now explain who supervises and who assesses a student midwife and how their roles fit together. You can also give constructive feedback, document performance well, and keep students within the law on medicines.

A.q: Under the NMC SSSA, who confirms that a student midwife has achieved her practice proficiencies?
options: The practice supervisor
The academic assessor
The practice assessor
The ward manager
A.why: SSSA 7.1–7.2: the practice assessor confirms achievement of practice proficiencies, informed by feedback from practice supervisors.

whyNot.0: Supervisors contribute observations but do not confirm proficiencies.
whyNot.1: The academic assessor confirms academic achievement.
whyNot.3: The ward manager has no assessing role under SSSA.

A.q: Who can act as practice assessor for a student midwife?
options: Any registered nurse on the unit
An NMC registered midwife
A registered obstetrician
A senior maternity support worker
A.why: SSSA 6.4: practice and academic assessors for midwifery students must be NMC registered midwives.

whyNot.0: A registered nurse may supervise but cannot assess a student midwife.
whyNot.2: An obstetrician may supervise but cannot be the practice assessor.
whyNot.3: Support workers are not registered professionals and cannot assess.

A.q: Which of these could act as a practice supervisor for a student midwife on the labour ward?
options: A registered obstetrician
A maternity support worker
A first-year student midwife
A doula supporting the woman
A.why: SSSA 2.7: supervision can be by NMC registered nurses, midwives, nursing associates and other registered health and social care professionals.

whyNot.1: Support workers are not registered professionals.
whyNot.3: A doula is not a registered health professional.

B.q: A student midwife asks to give intramuscular pethidine to a woman in labour with her supervisor watching. What is correct?
options: She may give it under direct supervision
She may give it if the woman consents
She may not give pethidine as a student
She may give it if she is in her final year
B.why: HMR 2012 Sch 17: student midwives may give the listed parenteral medicines under direct supervision except diamorphine, morphine and pethidine.

whyNot.0: Direct supervision applies to other Sch 17 medicines, not pethidine.
whyNot.1: Consent does not change the legal exclusion.
whyNot.3: Year of training does not change the exclusion.

B.q: A student midwife forgot to check a woman's identity before taking blood. What is the best way for her supervisor to give feedback?
options: Point it out in front of the woman
Save it for the final placement interview
Write it in the notes without telling her
Discuss it privately and specifically that day
B.why: Code 9.1 and SPM 5.21: feedback should be honest, constructive, timely, private and specific, with a plan.

whyNot.0: Public criticism is unkind and undermines the student.
whyNot.1: Delayed feedback gives her no chance to improve.
whyNot.2: She needs to know about it to learn.

B.q: A supervisor has concerns about a student's communication with women over several shifts. What should she do?
options: Record dated examples and tell the assessor
Wait a few more shifts to see if it improves
Ask other students to keep an eye on her
Suggest the women make formal complaints
B.why: SSSA 4.2–4.4: supervisors record observations, contribute to assessment and raise concerns, so the practice assessor can agree an action plan in time.

whyNot.1: Waiting leaves no time for an action plan.
whyNot.3: Concerns are raised by the supervisor, not passed to women.

C.q: A midwife is a student's practice assessor this placement and also wants to be her practice supervisor because they work the same shifts. What does the SSSA say?
options: It is allowed if the student agrees
It is allowed in the final placement
It is allowed with manager approval
The roles must be held by different people
C.why: SSSA 7.10: practice assessors are not simultaneously the practice supervisor and academic assessor for the same student, so these roles are held by different people.

whyNot.0: Student agreement does not override the standard.
whyNot.1: There is no final-placement exception for midwifery.
whyNot.2: Manager approval does not override the standard.

C.q: A student midwife moves from part 1 to part 2 of her programme. What happens to her academic assessor?
options: The same assessor continues throughout
A different academic assessor is nominated
Her practice assessor takes on the role
No academic assessor is needed in part 2
C.why: SSSA 6.1: a different academic assessor is nominated for each part of the programme.

whyNot.0: The SSSA requires a different academic assessor for each part.
whyNot.2: A practice assessor cannot simultaneously be the academic assessor.
whyNot.3: Every part of the programme has an academic assessor.

C.q: A midwife asks a student to give IM oxytocin for the third stage and leaves to answer a call bell. What is wrong with this?
options: Oxytocin needs a prescription for students
Students must be under direct supervision
Students may not give any injections
Doctors give third-stage oxytocin
C.why: HMR 2012 Sch 17: student midwives may give listed medicines such as oxytocins only under the direct supervision of a registered midwife, who must be present.

whyNot.0: Oxytocins are covered by the midwives' exemption, which includes students under direct supervision.
whyNot.2: Students may give listed injections under direct supervision.
whyNot.3: Midwives give third-stage oxytocin under the exemption.

reteach.title: Coach, referee, university official
reteach.question: Who does what when a student midwife is assessed?

blocks.body: The practice supervisor is the coach: teaches, demonstrates, feeds back and records what she sees. The practice assessor is the referee for practice: decides whether proficiencies are met, using the coaches' records. The academic assessor is the university official: confirms academic work and agrees progression with the practice assessor. For midwifery students, both assessors are midwives.

blocks.text: Supervisors can be any registered professional; assessors of student midwives must be registered midwives.

explain.body: SSSA 9.1: the academic assessor collates and confirms the student's achievement of academic outcomes, and works with the practice assessor to recommend progression.

test.q: What does the academic assessor confirm for a student midwife?
options: Clinical skills on placement
Achievement of academic outcomes
Attendance at shifts
Completion of mandatory training
test.why: SSSA 9.1: the academic assessor confirms academic achievement; the practice assessor confirms practice proficiencies.

whyNot.0: Clinical proficiencies are confirmed by the practice assessor.
whyNot.2: Attendance is monitored by the programme, not the academic assessor's confirmation role.
whyNot.3: Mandatory training is not the academic assessor's confirmation role.

explain.body: Practice supervisors record relevant observations on the student's conduct, proficiency and achievement, which inform the practice assessor's decisions.

test.q: How do practice supervisors contribute to a student midwife's assessment?
options: By signing off her practice proficiencies
By deciding her progression to next part
By setting her academic grade for the part
By recording observations for the assessor
test.why: SSSA 4.2–4.3: supervisors record observations and contribute to assessment, informing the practice assessor.

whyNot.0: Signing off is the practice assessor's role.
whyNot.1: Progression is recommended by both assessors together.
whyNot.2: Academic grading is the university's role.

explain.body: SPM 5.21 includes promoting reflection. Ask open questions: what went well, what was difficult, what would you do differently, what will you read up on?

test.q: Which question from a supervisor best promotes a student's reflection after a birth?
options: Did you enjoy being at that birth?
Was that the first birth you have seen?
What would you do differently next time?
Have you finished writing the notes yet?
test.why: Open questions about learning and future action promote reflection, as SPM 5.21 requires.

whyNot.0: A yes or no question about enjoyment does not prompt analysis.
whyNot.1: This is a factual question, not reflective.
whyNot.3: This checks a task rather than prompting reflection.

explain.body: Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001 art 45: only a registered midwife or medical practitioner may attend a woman in childbirth, except in sudden or urgent necessity or as a student on a recognised course of training.

test.q: Under the Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001, why may a student midwife attend a woman in childbirth?
options: She is on a recognised training course
She holds a first aid certificate
She has the woman's written consent
She has completed her first year
test.why: Art 45: attending a woman in childbirth is restricted to registered midwives and doctors, except in urgent necessity or for students on recognised training.

whyNot.1: First aid certification is not the legal basis.
whyNot.2: Consent does not create the legal exception.
whyNot.3: Year of study is not the legal basis.
